title: Autism Spectrum Disorder: Early Recognition and Developmental Referral

evidenceAudit.scope: Recognition of possible autism in children and young people and referral to a multidisciplinary autism team.
findings: Rebuilt against the approved-topic structure: a tiered investigation panel, time-ordered management and an explicit medicine decision pathway.
Every investigation row includes a reference or normal state, condition finding and next action.
Previous outline and published rows remain preserved; this additive version is pending clinical review.
unverifiedSections: No topic-specific Saudi national guideline was found in the opened Saudi Ministry of Health protocol index unless a Saudi source is explicitly cited in the medicine row.
Current live Saudi Food and Drug Authority product registration was not individually confirmed; clinicians must check the hospital formulary.
Local antibiogram, resistance pattern, shared-care agreement and imaging availability require site-level confirmation where relevant.

pathophysiology.summary: Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition characterised by differences in social communication and restricted or repetitive patterns. Presentation varies with age, language, cognition, sex, culture and environment. Coexisting developmental, neurological and mental-health needs often determine urgency and support.
keyMechanisms: Autism is a neurodevelopmental condition characterised by differences in social communication and restricted or repetitive patterns.
Presentation varies with age, language, cognition, sex, culture and environment.
Coexisting developmental, neurological and mental-health needs often determine urgency and support.

references.title: NICE CG128: Autism spectrum disorder in under 19s—recognition, referral and diagnosis

symptoms: Differences in reciprocal interaction, communication, flexibility, sensory responses or play.
physicalSigns: Restricted or repetitive behaviour, unusual sensory interests, developmental regression or uneven developmental profile.
redFlags: Developmental regression, new seizures, acute loss of function, self-harm, severe feeding restriction or safeguarding concern needs urgent parallel assessment.
precipitants: Increasing social, communication or sensory demands may make differences more apparent.

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Language impairment without the same persistent social reciprocity and restricted-pattern profile.
Abnormal hearing assessment may explain apparent response or language difficulty.
Broad delay across domains; autism can coexist and still requires assessment.
Activity and attention symptoms predominate, though both conditions can coexist.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Consider reported or observed features, duration, severity, settings, impact, developmental history and parental concern; do not rule out autism because one expected feature is absent (CG128 1.2–1.4).

ruleIn.normalValue: Age-appropriate reciprocal social communication and flexible behaviour
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Persistent social-communication differences with restricted or repetitive behaviour
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Integrates developmental history, observation and information across settings.

ruleIn.normalValue: Milestones achieved in the expected sequence without regression
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Delay, uneven profile or loss of previously acquired skills
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Regression changes urgency and the differential diagnosis.

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Consistent qualitative differences in interaction, communication or behaviour
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Do not rely on one brief encounter or one screening tool.
Excludes a remediable contributor to communication difficulty.
Identifies a sensory cause or comorbidity that changes support.

ruleIn.normalValue: No focal neurology, dysmorphism or abnormal head growth
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Neurological sign, dysmorphism or growth abnormality
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Directs genetic, neurological or metabolic referral.

ruleOut.expectedFinding: Pathogenic or likely pathogenic finding relevant to the phenotype
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Use when the multidisciplinary team identifies dysmorphism, intellectual disability or a syndrome pattern.
Not routine for autism; use for suspected epilepsy or episodic regression.

clinicalManagement.title: Record concern and immediate needs
actions: Take the concern seriously and describe observed features, development, function and settings.
Address hearing, sleep, feeding, education, mental health and safeguarding in parallel.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer to the autism pathway
clinicalManagement.timeframe: When features and impact warrant assessment
actions: Provide developmental history and reports from home and education.
Refer urgently for regression or other red flags through the appropriate neurological or paediatric pathway.

clinicalManagement.title: Support while waiting
actions: Offer needs-led adjustments and family support without waiting for a diagnostic label.
Share information with consent and name the professional coordinating the pathway.

medicationPlan.note: Do not use medication for the core features of autism. Treat epilepsy, sleep disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, anxiety or severe behaviour only through the relevant separate condition-specific pathway.

teaching.scope: Recognition of possible autism in children and young people and referral to a multidisciplinary autism team.
learningObjectives: Recognise the condition and its red flags.
Choose initial tests without delaying urgent escalation.
Use a named multidisciplinary disposition plan.
keyPoints: Developmental regression, new seizures, acute loss of function, self-harm, severe feeding restriction or safeguarding concern needs urgent parallel assessment.
Offer needs-led adjustments and family support without waiting for a diagnostic label.
pitfalls: Stopping after a short outline instead of documenting the full investigation pathway.
Using a medicine row without checking the branch, allergy, organ function, culture result and local formulary.
Mistaking publication status for clinical approval; this version remains pending until a clinician approves it.

patientEducation: Explain the working diagnosis, immediate plan and specific return or deterioration signs.
lifestyleAndDiet: Address prevention and self-management only after the acute safety plan is complete.
dischargeCriteria: Immediate risks addressed; referral accepted or alternative plan documented; family given a named contact and safety advice.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Track referral outcome and support needs; do not leave education, feeding, sleep or safeguarding needs pending solely because diagnosis is pending.
